ins:
The Rev. Calvin Swain 
(1778-1856) filed the first land claim in what is now Brooklyn on June 16, 1832. A chaplain in the War of 1812, Swain was a Baptist minister and postmaster in Adamsville, New York, before coming to Michigan. By 1833 he had established a settlement and a sawmill here. He was the postmaster until 1841. The town was called Swainsville until a town meeting adopted the name Brooklyn on August 5, 1836. Swain founded Baptist churches in Brooklyn, Woodstock, and Napoleon. He is buried in Oak Grove Cemetery in Napoleon.

ph.alt: Individuals standing in front of a single post marker with a building behind it.

ins: Thirteen lay members founded the First Presbyterian Church of Brooklyn in 1838. The Reverend C. W. Gurney became the church’s first installed pastor in 1841.  Dedicatory services for the church were held on October 7, 1845.  Built with hand-hewn beams and pegged timber, this is now the oldest church building in Brooklyn.  The original simple Greek Revival structure with its square belfry measured forty by sixty feet.  The church was remodeled in 1901 and enlarged twice in subsequent years.
